correctness.rationale: The actual package constructs an exact finite-state recognizer for deletion distance at most one, determinizes it to 11 states, and takes the three-pair product with 287 reachable states. The inspected verifier does not infer from a finite table: it certifies invariant Krylov spaces of dimensions 5 and 14 and annihilating polynomials \((t-2)^3(t-1)\) and \((t-2)^4(t-1)^3\), thereby proving the pair and ordered-triple recurrences for all lengths. Inclusion--exclusion removes coordinate equalities and division by six converts ordered distinct triples to triangles. Independently, I rebuilt the literal deletion graph for every \(1\le n\le7\); the triangle counts \(0,2,18,100,432,1592,5268\) exactly match the formula.

final_claim: For the binary one-deletion confusability graph \(\Gamma_{n,1}\), the number of unordered triangles is \[T_n=\frac{2^n(n^3+n^2-6n-28)+16(n^2+n+2)}8\] for every \(n\ge1\).
limitations: Binary alphabet and one deletion only.
